Translation of a proclamation, dated August 28, 1941, isued
in the name of Pan Dah, Commissioner of the Shanghai
Western Area Special Police Force, 57 Great Western Road.

August 28, 1941.

The protection of the people being the first duty of
the Special Police Force, I, the Commissioner, have, since my
assumption of office about half a year ago, spared no efforts
in performing this duty. It has now come to my knowledge that
persons are making the unlawful practice of demanding money from
factories under the pretext that they will give protection,
and further that ignorant merchants have proved to be easy prey
in their hands. I, who am strictly enforcing the law, cannot
tolerate the existence of such bad elements in this area and
will punish them severely when such cases are proved. All
people are expected to render assistance in suppressing crimes
of this nature and to make reports and submit evidence to this
Police Headquarters in a confidential manner. Informants
will not be involved in any trouble and they should have no
fear at all.

(Sealed) PAN DAH

Unrest Ended
Adjustment In
Pay Granted
Western Police

Ending all unrest in the ranks
of the Western District Special
Police, a large salary increase
was yesterday granted to the
City Government-paid con-
stables of the force, bringing
their wage standard closer to
parity with that of the con-
stables transferred from the
S.M.P.

The monthly pay of the con-
stables previously serving in the
City Government Police was raised,
from $30 to $93. This was still
lower than the $165 paid to the
former S.M.P. men, but according
to officials of the Western Area
Police force all men are now
satisfied.

The officials pointed out that the
former S.M.P. men are more
qualified than those of the City
Government, and therefore deserve
higher pay.

Previous reports claimed that the
former City Government policemen
had started a go-slow strike pend-
ing readjustment of their salaries.
Officials, however, denied this
report.

此前在市政府警察局服役的警员月薪从30元提高到93元。这仍低于前工部局警务处人员获得的165元，但据沪西警察部队官员称，目前所有人员均已满意。

官员们指出，前工部局警务处人员比市政府的人员资格更高，因此应获得更高的薪酬。

此前的报道声称，前市政府警察已开始怠工罢工，等待薪资调整。然而，官员们否认了这一报道。

May 5, 1941. Morning Translation

Cheng Yien Pao, Chinese-American Daily News, National Herald,
Shun Pao :-

POLICEMEN OF SPECIAL POLICE FORCE IN WESTERN DISTRICT
SUBMIT APPEAL

Recently, it was reported that the
policemen of the Special Police Force in the Western
District had asked for an increase of wages. Yesterday,
it was reported that the policemen would refuse to go on
duty until their demand was granted. However, it is now
learned that this threatened strike has been dropped.
There are in all 880 policemen attached to
the Special Police Force, 200 of whom were seconded from the
S.M.P. at a monthly wage of $165 each including allowances.
The rest were formerly policemen attached to the Police
Bureau and their wage is only $35 per mensem. In view of the
high cost of living, this pay is insufficient for the
maintenance of a lowest grade of livelihood. For this
reason, the policemen formerly attached to the Police
Bureau asked for an increase of their wages and for
similar treatment. As the Special Police Force failed
to give a reply, it was reported on the evening of May 3
that the policemen would refuse to go on duty on the
morning of May 4.
According to the Zoen Wen News Agency,
some 600 policemen of the Special Police Force submitted
an appeal to Pan Dah, Chief of the Force, on the morning
of May 4 and requested a reply.

Of the Council for the Foreign Settlement of Shanghai
Vol. XXXIV SHANGHAI, WEDNESDAY, FEBRUARY 12, 1941. 1829

REGULATIONS
Governing The Structure Of The Western Shanghai
Area Special Police Force.

(Signed at the Civic Centre, Kiangwan, on February 1, 1941.)

1. These Regulations with 3 appendices are agreed to and recommended by the Chief of the Police Bureau and the Commissioner of the Shanghai Municipal Police in accordance with paragraph 2 of the Modus Vivendi on Policing concluded between the City Government of Greater Shanghai (Shanghai Municipal Government) and the Shanghai Municipal Council on the sixteenth day of February, Nineteen Hundred and Forty.

2. The Western Shanghai Area Special Police Force will organize an institution known as the “Western Shanghai Area Special Police Force” (滬西特別警察總署) to control the area adjacent to the International Settlement and French Concession and the whole area formerly coming under the jurisdiction of West Shanghai Division and a section of the District coming under the jurisdiction of the Zikawei Police Division. The area will be divided into 5 Police Divisions (see map attached). The area under the jurisdiction of the Western Shanghai Area Special Police Force will include the districts at present guarded by the Shanghai Foreign Defence Forces.

3. The Western Shanghai Area Special Police Force shall be composed of the existing Police Main Corps, the whole West Shanghai Division, a part of the Zikawei Division and the Officers of the Detective Branch Corps, together with Officers recommended by the Municipal Council. The Force shall be the only organization to exercise Police powers in the Area concerned and shall be supervised and directed by the Chief of the Shanghai Municipal Police Bureau in accordance with the instructions of the Shanghai Municipal Government.

The maximum strength of the Special Police Force including the Officers recommended by the Municipal Council shall be 1,446 men with an additional reserve of 12 men, whose distributions are given in appended tables.

4. Uniforms: The style of the Uniform of the Western Shanghai Area Special Police Force will be in accordance with the normal requirements of the Shanghai Municipal Government.

A Hat Badge distinct from the normal Municipal Government Police will be designed with the superimposed Chinese and Foreign characters meaning “Special Police,” and worn by all ranks.

Roman Numerals as well as Chinese Numerals will be worn by all ranks below that of Sub-Inspector.

5. To meet emergencies and labour trouble, a Reserve Unit will be formed (see Appendix III).

The strength of the Force will not be increased or decreased without the agreement of the Shanghai Municipal Government and the Shanghai Municipal Council.

6. Under the Western Shanghai Area Special Police Force, there will be five Police Divisions, a number of Stations and Sub-Stations; one Commissioner whose title will be (總署長), and one Deputy Commissioner, whose title will be (副總署長), who will, in accordance with the instructions of their superior officer, supervise and direct Officers and men under their command.

条例
 governing 沪西特别警察部队之组织。

（1941年2月1日签署于江湾市民中心。）

1. 本条例及其三个附录，系根据1940年2月16日大上海市政府（上海特别市政府）与上海公共租界工部局之间达成的《警务临时协定》第二款，由警察局局长和上海公共租界工部局警务处处长同意并推荐。

2. 沪西特别警察部队将组建一个名为“沪西特别警察总队”（滬西特別警察總署）的机构，以管控与国际租界和法租界相邻的区域，以及原属西区分区管辖的全部区域和徐家汇警察分区管辖的部分区域。该区域将划分为5个警察分区（见附图）。沪西特别警察部队的管辖区域将包括目前由上海外侨防卫队守卫的地区。

3. 沪西特别警察部队应由现有的警察主力部队、整个西区分区、徐家汇分区的一部分以及侦探支队的警官组成，再加上由工部局推荐的警官。该部队将是有关区域内行使警察权力的唯一组织，并根据上海特别市政府的指示，受上海公共租界工部局警察局局长的监督和指导。

特别警察部队的最高编制人数，包括由工部局推荐的警官，为1,446人，另加12人的后备储备，其分布见附表。

4. 制服：沪西特别警察部队的制服样式将符合上海特别市政府的常规要求。

将设计一种不同于市政府常规警察的帽徽，上面叠加含义为“特别警察”的中外文文字，并由所有级别人员佩戴。

副督察以下的所有级别人员将佩戴罗马数字以及中文数字标识。

5. 为应对紧急情况和劳工纠纷，将组建一支后备分队（见附录三）。

未经上海特别市政府和上海公共租界工部局同意，不得增加或减少部队编制人数。

6. 在沪西特别警察部队之下，将设有五个警察分区、若干个分局和支局；一名总办，其职称为（總署長），以及一名副总办，其职称为（副總署長），他们将根据上级官员的指示，监督和指挥其下属的警官和警员。

The Divisional Branches are as follows:—

1st Division: Soochow Creek on the North, Settlement Boundary on the East. Jessfield Road (exclusive) on the South, Brenan Piece (exclusive) on the West.

2nd Division: Jessfield Road (inclusive) on the North, Settlement Boundary on the East. Avenue Haig on the South, Edinburgh Road (inclusive) on the West.

3rd Division: Soochow Creek on the North, Brenan Piece (inclusive) and Edinburgh Road (exclusive) on the East, Yu Yuen Road (exclusive) on the South. Railway (exclusive) on the West.

4th Division: Yu Yuen Road (inclusive) on the North, Edinburgh Road (exclusive) on the East. Great Western Road (inclusive) on the West.

5th Division: Great Western Road (exclusive) on the North. Edinburgh Road (exclusive) and Avenue Haig (inclusive) on the East. Hungjao (inclusive) on the South. Railway (exclusive) on the West.

The area to the west of the railway line will not be discussed owing to the general unsettled situation.

7. The administration of the Western Shanghai Area Special Police Force will include the following branches and their functions will be as under:—

Police Affairs Branch: This Branch will deal with affairs relating to personnel, training, official correspondence, official seals, editing, statistics, equipment, arms, files, receiving and despatching of official correspondence, accounts and general business, etc.

Executive Branch: This Branch will deal with affairs relating to the security of peace, maintenance of public morals, traffic, census, sanitation and assistance to Municipal Authorities.

Special Branch: This Branch will deal with affairs relating to the suppression of Communists, reactionaries, collection of intelligence, mediation in labour disputes and suppression of reactionary newspapers, magazines, publications and writings, etc.

Foreign Affairs Branch: This Branch will deal with affairs relating to the protection of life and property of Foreign Nationals, and their domicile and trade; and will also handle cases involving Foreign Nationals and deal with Foreign Police Officers.

Crime Branch: This Branch will deal with affairs relating to criminal investigation, breach of Police Regulations, detention or release of prisoners, examination of finger prints and photos, collection of evidence, etc.

Supervising Branch: This Branch will deal with affairs relating to the supervision of outdoor and indoor staffs.

Secretarial Office: This office will deal with confidential documents and keep records of all outside and interior correspondence.

8. In each Branch there will be one Officer in Charge, one Deputy and 6 to 10 Junior Officers.

In the Supervising Branch there will be a number of superintending Officers, whilst in the Secretarial Office there will be two secretaries. All of these Officers are under the supervision and direction of the Commissioner but the Officer in charge Police Affairs Branch in accordance with the instructions of the Commissioner shall have the authority to direct Divisional Officers. If the Officer in charge of a Branch is not a Municipal Council's nominee, the Deputy shall be selected from those nominated by the Shanghai Municipal Council.

9. In each Police Division of the Western Shanghai Area Special Police Force, there will be one Divisional Officer and one or two Deputies who will be under the supervision and direction of the Commissioner and take charge of the business of the Division.

10. At the request of either party, the Western Shanghai Area Special Police Force and the Shanghai Municipal Police, each will at all times render assistance in accordance with the modus vivendi made separately (Appendix I).

执行处：本处负责处理与治安、维护公共道德、交通、户口、卫生以及协助市政当局等相关事宜。

APPENDIX I.
AGREEMENT
For Close Cooperation Against The Criminal Element Between The Western Shanghai Area Special Police Force And The Shanghai Municipal Polices.
As it is essential in the public interest that criminals who commit crimes in one area, do not obtain safety in an adjacent area, it is suggested the following general provisions be agreed upon:—

Close Pursuit:
Any person committing a crime in the Western area, who runs or escapes into the Settlement or vice versa, and is closely pursued and arrested, will be taken to the nearest Police Station of the area in which the arrest is made for record only, and will be handed over direct and at once, while the Police concerned will be held in no way to blame for crossing the boundary.

Possession of Property Stolen:
Any person found in the Settlement in possession of property stolen from the Western Special Area, or vice versa, will be handed over to the Police Force controlling the area in which the property was stolen at once, as soon as particulars have been recorded at the appropriate Police Station.

Following up Cases of Serious Crime:
In the investigation of crime, when it is found by members of the Western Shanghai Area Special Police Force that confederates of a criminal gang are living or hiding in the area under the jurisdiction of the Municipal Police, the Police Station concerned will give immediate cooperation to the Officers in charge of such cases to effect the arrests of such criminals.
In the case of the following crimes, such persons when arrested will be handed over direct at once if there is reasonable suspicion that a true case exists:—
Armed Kidnapping; Abduction; Armed Robbery; Robbery; Threatening Letters; Intimidation; Murder or Attempted Murder.
The Western Shanghai Area Special Police Force will, within one week, report details of evidence against such accused to the Shanghai Municipal Police or will return accused to the custody of the Municipal Police or vice versa.
The Western Shanghai Area Special Police Force will afford similar facilities to the Shanghai Municipal Police under exactly similar conditions.
Such prisoners will, in every case, receive proper treatment within the law, and be returned, if not charged, in good condition. Such prisoners will not be detained more than 24 hours without going to Court.
Persons committing crimes in the Western Area shall be handed over direct to the Shanghai District Court to be dealt with according to law.

Following Up Other Crimes:
The direct handling over of suspects in less serious crimes will be ruled by the public interest, and in accordance with the evidence available.
In carrying out the above, much will depend on goodwill and a sincere desire to combine against the criminal element and every effort must be made to follow the spirit as well as the letter of the understanding, while any attempt to misuse these provisions for cooperation can only result in a state of affairs harmful to the public whom it is our duty to protect.

APPENDIX II.
Relations Of The Commissioner And Deputy Commissioner.
(A) The Commissioner, in accordance with the instructions of his superior, will be responsible for the supervision and direction of his subordinate Officers and men, whilst the Deputy Commissioner, in accordance with the instructions of his superior, will assist the Commissioner in a friendly and cooperative spirit in dealing with all matters in the area. The Deputy Commissioner shall be responsible to the Commissioner for the handling of all daily routine matters but must first refer such matters to the Commissioner for his examination and signature before execution.

附录一。
协议
关于上海西区特别警察队与上海公共租界工部局警务处之间针对犯罪分子的紧密合作。
鉴于为了公共利益，必须确保在一个区域作案的罪犯无法在相邻区域获得庇护，兹建议就以下一般条款达成一致：—

紧密追捕：
任何在西区作案后逃入租界，或反之从租界逃入西区并遭到紧追而被捕的人员，仅会被带至逮捕地所属区域的最近警察局进行登记，随后将立即直接移交；相关警察人员因越界行动而不承担任何责任。

持有被盗财物：
任何在租界内被发现持有从西区特别区盗窃的财物者，或反之在西区特别区持有从租界盗窃的财物者，一旦在相应警察局记录详情后，将立即移交给失窃财物所在区域的管辖警察部队。

重案跟进：
在犯罪调查中，当上海西区特别警察队成员发现犯罪团伙的同伙居住或藏匿于工部局警务处管辖区域内时，相关警察局应立即配合负责此类案件的警官，以实施对该等罪犯的逮捕。
对于下列犯罪，如有合理怀疑案件属实，被捕人员将立即直接移交：—
武装绑架；拐骗；武装抢劫；抢劫；恐吓信；胁迫；谋杀或谋杀未遂。
上海西区特别警察队将在一周内，向上海公共租界工部局警务处报告针对此类被告的证据细节，或将被告交还工部局警务处羁押，反之亦然。
上海西区特别警察队将在完全相同的条件下，为上海公共租界工部局警务处提供类似的便利。
此类囚犯在所有情况下均将依法得到适当对待，若未被起诉，将以良好状态归还。此类囚犯未经法庭审理，拘留时间不得超过24小时。
在西区作案的人员应直接移交至上海特区法院，依法处理。

其他犯罪跟进：
较轻罪行嫌疑人的直接移交，将依据公共利益及现有证据决定。
在执行上述规定时，很大程度上取决于善意以及联合打击犯罪分子的真诚愿望；必须尽力遵循该谅解的精神及条文，任何企图滥用这些合作条款的行为，只会导致损害我们要保护的公众利益的局面。

附录二。
局长与副局长的关系。
(A) 局长将根据其上级的指示，负责监督和指导其下属警官及警员；而副局长将根据其上级的指示，以友好合作的精神协助局长处理辖区内的所有事务。副局长负责处理所有日常例行事务，但在执行前必须先将此类事务呈报局长审查并签字。

APPENDIX III.
RESERVE UNIT
Western Shanghai Area Special Police Force.

In order to suppress riots or disturbances and labour troubles in the area under its control a Reserve Unit will be formed within the Western Shanghai Area Special Police Force with the following personnel:—

1 Officer in charge.
1 Deputy.
3 Officers in charge of squads.
2 Clerks.
9 Sergeants and 62 Constables.
Total—78 men.

When called out to riot or disturbance, Foreign and Japanese members of the Foreign Affairs Branch will accompany the Unit, if Foreign interests are involved.

Duties:
(1) To quell riots or disturbances.
(2) To take emergency precautions.
(3) To maintain order on the spot.
(4) To effect the arrest of robbers and bandits.
(5) To search pedestrians.
(6) To reinforce police beats.

The Unit will be available at any time during 24 hours at strength not less than 1 Senior Officer and 50 other ranks.

Equipment:
The Unit will carry batons, rifles and will be trained in Riot Drill.
Axes and crowbars for breaking in doors will be carried with the transport.

Operations:
The Unit will operate under the orders of the Commissioner and under the direction of the Deputy Commissioner, but when despatched to Divisions to assist in their functions, it will be placed under the direction of the Officer in charge of the Division concerned.

附录三。
预备队
上海西区特别警察队。

为了镇压其管辖区域内的暴乱、骚动及劳资纠纷，上海西区特别警察队内将组建一支预备队，人员编制如下：—

1名主管警官。
1名副手。
3名小队主管警官。
2名文员。
9名巡长和62名巡捕。
总计—78人。

当出动应对暴乱或骚动时，若涉及外国利益，外事科的外国籍和日本籍成员将随队行动。

职责：
(1) 平息暴乱或骚动。
(2) 采取紧急预防措施。
(3) 维持现场秩序。
(4) 实施对强盗和匪徒的逮捕。
(5) 搜查行人。
(6) 增援巡逻岗。

该队在24小时内随时待命，兵力不少于1名高级警官和50名其他职级人员。

装备：
该队将配备警棍、步枪，并接受防暴操练训练。
用于破门的斧头和撬棍将随运输车辆携带。

行动：
该队将在局长的命令和副局长的指挥下行动，但当被派往各分区协助其职能时，将受相关分区主管警官的指挥。

SPECIAL ANNEX.

As soon as the Western Shanghai Area Special Police Force has been organized and established and commences to function in accordance with the Chinese law, all illegitimate businesses (such as the running of gambling dens, trafficking in opium and narcotics and providing addicts with such narcotics) shall be forbidden to exist within the area under its jurisdiction.

All illegitimate and unlawful businesses shall be ordered to cease with the inauguration of the Western Shanghai Area Special Police Force and the commencement of the discharge of its functions. Any attempt to resume such activities shall at once be strictly suppressed.

May Be Threshed Out, Says Domei Report;

RIGHT TO COLLECT TAXES, RATES IN
WESTERN DISTRICT BEING STUDIED

With a satisfactory solution to the Western Area policing
problem having been reached with formal signatures to a
detailed agreement signed by Mr. Chen Kung-po, Mayor of the
Shanghai Municipal Government and Mr. W. J. Keswick, Chair-
man of the Shanghai Municipal Council, there are bright pros-
pects for an end to all arguments over this long standing issue,
political observers declared yesterday.

These circles recalled that not
only the police question but other,
even more important matters, re-
lating to this area of Shanghai,
which were aggravating problems
during the days of the former
National Government under Gen-
eral Chiang Kai-shek, are likely
to be solved soon to the satisfac-
tion of all parties concerned, states
a Domei report.
These same problems and policies
towards the International Settle-
ment and French Concession of
Shanghai were under negotiation
in 1937 when the Sino-Japanese
hostilities broke out but had to be
abandoned by the Chiang Kai-
shek Government which withdrew
to Chungking.

Backed By Japanese

Strongly backed by the Japa[n]ese
authorities, the reconstructed
Shanghai Special Municipal Gov-
ernment again launched negotia-
tions for a solution with the
Shanghai Municipal Council which
solely ex[i]sts through established
influence of Britons and Americans,
according to the report.
However, three years were to
elapse during which negotiations
were in progress and during which
time high tension frequently
prevailed and numerous bloody
incidents occurred, the most notable
of which was the Sergeant Xinlock
incident in the British Defence
Sector.
With the outbreak of the
European War, these well-informed
circles declared, of the Shanghai
Municipal Council suddenly became
conciliatory, which led to opening
of talks between the late Mayor Fu
Siao-en and Mr. C. S. Franklin,
former Chairman of the Shang[hai]
Municipal Council, through the
offices of Mr. Yoshiaki Miura,
former Japanes[e] Consul-General,
and Commander Luigi Neyrone,
former Italian Consul-General.
Both parties last February reach-
ed a modus vivendi agreement
leading up to the present formal
accord through Mr. Chen Kung-po.
General administrative questions
including the right of levying taxes
and rates are still in a negotiator[y]
stage, however, and no complete
understanding has been reached on
these issues, the Domei report adds.

Police Agreement
Satisfactory
Further Negotiations
Foreshadowed to Domei
News Agency

With a satisfactory solution to the Western Area policing problem having been reached with formal signatures to a detailed agreement signed by Mr. Chen Kung-po, Mayor of the Shanghai Municipal Government, and Mr. W. J. Keswick, Chairman of the Shanghai Municipal Council, there are bright prospects for an end to all arguments over this long-standing issue, political observers declared to Domei yesterday.

These circles recalled that not only the police question but other, even more important matters, relating to this area of Shanghai, which were aggravating problems during the days of the former National Government, under General Chiang Kai-shek, are likely to be solved soon to the satisfaction of all parties concerned.

These same problems and policies towards the International Settlement and French Concession of Shanghai were under negotiation in 1937 when the Sino-Japanese hostilities broke out, but had to be abandoned by the Chiang Kai-shek Government which withdrew to Chungking.

Strong Japanese Backing

Strongly backed by the Japanese authorities, the reconstructed Shanghai Special Municipal Government again launched negotiations for a solution with the Shanghai Municipal Council.

However, three years were to elapse during which negotiations were in progress during which time high tension frequently prevailed and numerous incidents occurred.

With the outbreak of the European War, these well-informed circles declared to Domei, the attitude of the Shanghai Municipal Council suddenly became conciliatory and which led to opening of talks between the late Mayor Fu Siao-an and Mr. C. S. Franklin, former Chairman of the Shanghai Municipal Council, through the good offices of Mr. Yoshiaki Miura, former Japanese Consul-General, and Comdr. Luigi Neyrone, former Italian Consul-General.

Both parties last February reached a modus vivendi agreement leading up to the present formal accord through Mr. Chen Kung-po.

General administrative questions including the right of levying taxes and rates are still in a negotiatory stage, however, and no complete understanding has been reached on these issues.

A WELCOME STEP

After an interval of just one year the modus vivendi concerning the policing of the Western Area, which was reached last February, has been supplemented by a full agreement between the Shanghai Municipal Government and the Shanghai Municipal Council, which it is hoped will settle once and for all the many questions which have been outstanding all too long, and establish means for restoring order in the "Badlands." The agreement goes into considerable detail regarding the formation of the new police force and a system has been evolved which should prove completely workable. Attached to the agreement are three appendices and one special annex, which are of the utmost importance. In the first there is provision for "close pursuit" which reads:—

Any person committing a crime in the Western Area, who runs, or escapes into the Settlement, or vice versa, and is closely pursued and arrested, will be taken to the nearest police station of the area in which the arrest is made for record only, and will be handed over direct and at once, while the Police concerned will be held in no way to blame for crossing the boundary.

This important provision should serve to remove difficulties which have arisen in the past out of conflict of police jurisdiction, and should serve to rob criminals of that asylum which could easily be secured merely by dodging across the boundaries.

The same appendix provides for close co-operation in dealing with possession of stolen property and the following ' ' of serious cases of crime, and tends to give the Settlement and Western Area Police a degree of mobility which has hitherto not existed, and while they will each maintain their separate identity, they will in fact become practically one single unit when dealing with criminals. This should ultimately have the effect of putting a stranglehold on those criminals who, using the Western Area as their base, operate in the International Settlement taking refuge outside the limits and making it difficult for the Municipal Police to go after them.

That will indeed be a welcome change, but the provisions of the special annex are even more so:—

As soon as the Western Shanghai Area Special Police Force has been organized and established and commences to function in accordance with the Chinese law, all illegitimate businesses (such as the running of gambling dens, trafficking in opium and narcotics and providing addicts with such narcotics) shall be forbidden to exist within the area under its jurisdiction.

All illegitimate and unlawful business shall be ordered to cease with the inauguration of the Western Special Police Force and the commencement of the discharge of its functions. Any attempt to resume such activities shall at once be strictly suppressed.

If the intention expressed in this annex is carried into effect, and it is to be believed that it will be, then the end of all that makes conditions in the Western Area so deplorable may be said to be in sight. It may be that those interests deriving profit from the illicit gambling dens will offer resistance to the stopping of their very remunerative enterprise, but the Shanghai Municipal Government should be able with the assistance of the new police force to put a stop to activities which are clearly illegal, and doing an enormous amount of harm.

It is to be hoped that there will be no further delays in putting the scheme into operation, and that every effort will be made to bring the special police force into being as quickly as possible. That subversive elements may seek to prevent that being done may be taken for granted, but the worth of this most important document can only be measured by the manner in which its terms are carried out. If that is done to the bitter end, then a substantial reform will have been effected and the Alsatia of rogues and criminals will become a thing of the past. For the rest congratulations are to be extended to Major K. M. Bourne, M.C., Commissioner of the Shanghai Municipal Police, and General Loo Ying, Commissioner of the Police Bureau of the Shanghai Municipal Government, for the successful result which has attended their negotiations over the past year, and also to the Authorities,—and particularly Mayor Chen Kung-po whose assistance has been most useful,—whose signatures are now appended to the agreement. The removal of a frequent cause of misunderstandings in the past is a step in the right direction, providing a chance for further co-operation between the two jurisdictions.

可喜的一步

就在去年二月达成关于西区警务的临时安排（modus vivendi）整整一年之后，上海市政府与上海公共租界工部局之间又达成了一项全面协议。人们希望这项协议能一劳永逸地解决那些悬而未决已久的问题，并建立恢复“恶土”（Badlands）秩序的手段。该协议就新警察部队的组建作了相当详细的规定，并制定了一套被证明完全可行的制度。协议附有三个附录和一个特别附件，它们至关重要。第一个附录中规定了“紧追”条款，内容如下：—

凡在西区犯罪后逃跑或逃入租界者，反之亦然，若被紧追并逮捕，仅将被带至逮捕地所属区域的最近警察局进行登记，并立即直接移交；有关警察人员越界执法不承担任何责任。

这一重要规定应能消除过去因警察管辖权冲突而产生的困难，并使犯罪分子无法再仅仅通过躲过边界线就能轻易获得庇护。

同一附录还规定在处理持有赃物及下列严重犯罪案件时要密切合作，这倾向于赋予租界警察和西区警察以前所没有的一定程度的机动性；虽然他们各自保持独立的身份，但在对付罪犯时，实际上将成为一个单一的整体。这最终将对那些以西区为基地、在国际租界内活动、作案后逃出租界范围从而使工部局警察难以追捕的罪犯形成扼制之势。

这确实是一个可喜的变化，但特别附件的规定更令人欢迎：—

一旦上海西区特别警察部队按照中国法律组织成立并开始运作，其管辖区域内禁止存在一切非法营业（如开设赌场、贩卖鸦片和麻醉品以及向吸食者提供此类麻醉品）。

所有非法和违法的营业应在西区特别警察部队成立并开始履行职能之时停止。任何企图恢复此类活动的行为将立即受到严厉镇压。

如果本附件中所表达的意图得以实施——相信它会得以实施——那么可以说，导致西区状况如此糟糕的一切根源已可见终结之日。那些从非法赌场获利的利益集团可能会对停止这种利润丰厚的企业活动进行抵制，但上海市政府在新警察部队的协助下，应能够制止这些明显非法且造成巨大危害的活动。

希望该方案的实施不再拖延，并将尽一切努力尽快组建特别警察部队。颠覆分子可能会试图阻止此事，这是可以预料的，但这份最重要文件的价值只能以其条款的执行方式来衡量。如果能坚持到底，则将实现实质性的改革，流氓和罪犯的避难所（Alsatia）将成为过去。此外，谨向上海公共租界工部局警务处处长 K. M. Bourne 少校（M.C.）和上海市政府警察局局长陆英将军表示祝贺，他们在过去一年的谈判中取得了成功的结果；同时也向当局——特别是陈公博市长，他的协助极为有益——表示祝贺，他们的名字现已签署在协议上。消除过去经常引起误解的一个原因，是朝着正确方向迈出的一步，为两个管辖区之间的进一步合作提供了机会。

Signed at Civic Centre

Gambling Dens and Illegitimate Business Must
Cease ; Galaxy of Officials Attend Ceremony

THE Western Area Police Agreement, an accord aimed at the
restoration of order out of chaos in the most troublous area in
Shanghai was signed at 10 a.m. yesterday at the Kiangwan Civic
Centre by Mr. W. J. Keswick, Chairman of the Shanghai Municipal
Council, and Mayor Chen Kung-po of the Shanghai Municipal
Government.

A comprehensive and detailed document for the immediate
establishment of a police force in the territory concerned, the
agreement was concluded after long-drawn-out negotiations
between the authorities of the Settlement and the Shanghai Muni-
cipal Government.

Among those present were Mr. G.
Godfrey Phillips, Secretary and Com-
missioner-General of the Council;
Maj. K. M. Bourne, Commissioner of
the Shanghai Municipal Police; and
Mr. H. Ibusuki, Japanese Deputy-
Secretary of the Council who arrived
with Mr. Keswick; Mr. R. T. Bryan,
Jun., Municipal Advocate, and Mr. T.
Beesley, Publicity Officer of the
Council who were earlier arrivals:
General Loo Ying, Police Commis-
sioner of the Shanghai Municipal
Government; Mr. Kimpson Yu, sec-
retary of the mayor who arrived with
the mayoral party, and other Chinese
officials.

Short Ceremony

Mayor Chen sat at one desk and
Mr. Keswick at another when the
texts of the agreement were signed
after which the party adjourned to
an adjoining room where champagne
was served to the guests. The en-
tire ceremony lasted about 20
minutes.

Following the conclusion of a
modus vivendi in February, 1940, out-
lining the principles governing the
establishment of a special police force
for the area exchanges of views were
made between Major Bourne and
General Loo Ying whose final agree-
ment was recently approved by a
Council majority. Under the regu-
lations for the formation of the new
force its members will wear a hat
badge with distinctive characters de-
noting "Special Police."

Texts of the portentous document,
which sounds a death knell to all
gambling establishments in Shanghai's
notorious western area, in English
and Chinese and incorporate regula-
tions for the establishment of a
special police force to exercise vigil-
ance over the area which will be
divided into five police divisions and
which provides for a maximum per-
sonnel of 1,446 men (193 will be
seconded from the Municipal Police)
with an additional reserve of twelve
including the officers recommended
by the Municipal Council. The area
concerned is adjacent to the Settle-
ment and French Concession and the
entire territory which was formerly
under the jurisdiction of the West
Shanghai Division and a section of
the district under the jurisdiction of
the Zhawei police division and in-
cludes the districts now guarded by
the Shanghai Foreign Defence Forces.

Illicit Business to Cease

A special annex to the agreement
prohibits the conduct of all illegitim-
ate business in the area such as
gambling dens, resorts for smoking
opium and narcotics. The haunts of
vice which have flourished in the dis-
trict will be ordered to cease operat-
ing as soon as the new police force
begins functioning. Attempts to re-
sume operations later it was stated,
shall be strictly suppressed.

Provision is made for the appoint-
ment of a Chinese commissioner and
a European deputy commissioner to
be nominated by the Council. Cases
involving foreign nationals will be
handled under instructions of the de-
puty commissioner. In case of doubt
regarding the handling of any case
and where opposite views are held
by the commissioner and deputy com-
missioner, reference will be made in
writing to the Commissioner of
Police of the Shanghai Municipal
Government and the Commissioner of
the Shanghai Municipal Police for
decision failing which reference of
the case will be made to the Mayor
and the Chairman of the Municipal
Council.

Personnel Nominated by S.M.C.

Under the agreement the personnel
nominated by the Municipal Council
will include in addition to the deputy
commissioner in the Foreign Affairs
Branch a European officer in charge
and 27 junior officers including
seventeen Westerners, nine Japanese,
a Japanese deputy in charge and a
Chinese and a foreign junior officer
in the General Affair Branch; a Jap-
anese and a Western junior officers
in the Administration Branch; a
Japanese deputy in charge and two
officers, one Japanese and one West-
erner in the Special Branch; a for-
eign deputy in charge and a Chinese
and one Japanese junior officers in
the Supervising Branch. In the five
police divisions the Council will
nominate two officers in charge and
three deputies and in addition will
nominate 23 sub-inspectors, sixteen
sergeants and 110 Chinese constables.

Cases involving foreign nationals
with extrality rights will be handled
according to the national law con-
cerned and in all other cases Chinese
law will be applicable. The terms
of service of the men nominated by
the Council will be the same as
Council employees.

西区警察协定
在市中心签署

赌场和非法营业必须停止；众多官员出席仪式

旨在恢复上海最动荡地区混乱秩序的《西区警察协定》，于昨日上午10时在江湾市中心由上海公共租界工部局董事会主席 W. J. Keswick 先生和上海市政府市长陈公博签署。

这是一份关于在有关地区立即建立警察部队的全面而详细的文件，该协议是在租界当局与上海市政府经过长期谈判后达成的。

出席者包括：工部局秘书兼总办 G. Godfrey Phillips 先生；上海公共租界工部局警务处处长 K. M. Bourne 少校；日本籍工部局副秘书 H. Ibusuki 先生，他随 Keswick 先生一同抵达；市法律顾问 R. T. Bryan  Jr. 先生和工部局宣传官 T. Beesley 先生，他们较早到达；上海市政府警察局局长陆英将军；随市长一行抵达的市长秘书俞金普（Kimpson Yu，音译）先生以及其他中国官员。

简短的仪式

陈市长坐在一张办公桌前，Keswick 先生坐在另一张办公桌前，签署了协议文本。随后，众人移步至隔壁房间，向客人供应香槟。整个仪式持续了约20分钟。

继1940年2月达成概述该地区特别警察部队建立原则的临时安排之后，Bourne 少校和陆英将军交换了意见，其最终协议最近获得了工部局多数成员的批准。根据新部队的组建规定，其成员将佩戴标有“特别警察”独特字样的帽徽。

这份重要文件的英文和中文文本宣告了上海臭名昭著的西区所有赌博场所的终结，其中包含了建立特别警察部队对该地区进行警戒的规定。该地区将划分为五个警区，最高编制为1,446人（其中193人将从工部局警察部队借调），另有包括工部局推荐的警官在内的12名后备人员。有关地区毗邻租界和法租界，包括原属西上海分区管辖的全部领土以及闸北警察分区管辖的一部分地区，并包括目前由上海外侨防卫队（Shanghai Foreign Defence Forces）守卫的地区。

非法营业将停止

协议的一个特别附件禁止在该地区进行一切非法营业，如赌场、吸食鸦片和麻醉品的场所。一旦新警察部队开始运作，该区猖獗的罪恶窝点将被勒令停止运营。据称，日后任何企图恢复运营的行为都将受到严厉镇压。

协议规定任命一名由中国方面担任的局长和一名由工部局提名的欧洲籍副局长。涉及外国国民的案件将按照副局长的指示处理。如果在处理任何案件时存在疑问，且局长和副局长持有相反意见，将以书面形式提请上海市政府警察局局长和上海公共租界工部局警务处处长作出决定；若仍无法解决，则将该案提交市长和工部局董事会主席裁决。

由工部局提名的人员

根据协议，由工部局提名的人员除外事处的副局长外，还包括：一名欧洲籍主管警官和27名初级警官，其中有17名西方人、9名日本人、一名日本籍副主管，以及总务处的一名中国和一名外国初级警官；行政处的一名日本和一名西方初级警官；特务处的一名日本籍副主管和两名警官（一名日本人，一名西方人）；督察处的一名外国籍副主管以及一名中国和一名日本初级警官。在五个警区中，工部局将提名两名主管警官和三名副主管，此外还将提名23名副巡官、16名警长和110名中国巡捕。

涉及享有治外法权的外国国民的案件将根据有关国家法律处理，在所有其他案件中适用中国法律。由工部局提名的人员的服务条件将与工部局雇员相同。

(exclusive) on the east, Great Western
Road (inclusive) on the west.
5th Division:-Great Western Road
(exclusive) on the north, Edinburgh
Road (exclusive) and Avenue Haig (in-
clusive) on the east, Hungjao (inclu-
sive) on the south, Railway (exclusive)
on the west.

The area to the west of the rail-
way line was not discussed owing to
the general unsettled situation.

Closer Police Co-operation

After dealing with the functions of
the respective branches and its per-
sonnel the agreement provides for the
exchange of assistance when request-
ed and required between the new
police force and the Municipal Police
each force to have a liaison officer
with three assistants to cope with
exchange of intelligence, to conduct
co-ordinated searches and extradition
of suspects and assist in the satisfac-
tory solution of diplomatic cases.

A number of the staff of the new
force, under the agreement, and
officers in charge of divisions where
a majority of residents are foreigners
owning factories, shops and property
in the area, if deemed necessary, will
be appointed from candidates recom-
mended by the Municipal Council.
No police officer or clerk previously
dismissed or resigned from the Muni-
cipal Police for improper conduct will
be eligible for employment in the new
force. This applies also to persons
previously convicted of a criminal
offence or who have been dismissed
from the French police, also the
Shanghai Municipal Police will not
employ men discharged in future
from the new force. Chinese shall
be the official language of the new
force to be used on all its official
documents.

Incorporated in the agreement are
three appendices and the special
annex dealing with the suppression
of illegitimate business in the district
within the jurisdiction of the new
force. The first appendix provides
for closer co-operation between the
new force and the Settlement police
as follows:

Principles of Co-operation

As it is essential in the public in-
terest, states Appendix 1, that crimin-
als who commit crimes in one area
do not obtain safety in an adjacent
area, it is suggested the following
general provisions be agreed upon:-

Any person committing a crime in
the Western area, who runs or escapes
into the Settlement or vice versa
and is closely pursued and arrested,
will be taken to the nearest Police
Station of the area in which the ar-
rest is made for record only, and will
be handed over direct and at once
while the Police concerned will be
held in no way to blame for crossing
the boundary.

Any person found in the Settlement
in possession of property stolen from
the Western Special Area, or vice
versa, will be handed over to the
Police Force controlling the area in
which the property was stolen, at
once, as soon as particulars have been
recorded at the appropriate Police
Station.

In the investigation of crime, when
it is found by members of the West-
ern Shanghai Area Special Police
Force that confederates of a criminal
gang are living or hiding in the area
under the jurisdiction of the Muni-
cipal Police, the Police Station con-
cerned will give immediate coopera-
tion to the officers in charge of such
cases to effect the arrests of such
criminals.

In the case of the following crimes,
such persons when arrested will be
handed over direct at once if there
is reasonable suspicion that a true
case exists:-armed kidnapping;
seduction; armed robbery; robbery;
threatening letters; intimidation; mur-
der or attempted murder.

Persons committing crimes in the
Western Area shall be handed over
direct to the Shanghai District Court
to be dealt with according to law.

The direct handing over of sus-
pects in less serious crimes will be
ruled by the public interest, and in
accordance with the evidence avail-
able.

In carrying out the above, much
will depend on goodwill and a sincere
desire to combine against the criminal
element and every effort must be
made to follow the spirit as well as
the letter of the understanding, while
any attempt to misuse those pro-
visions for cooperation can only re-
sult in a state of affairs harmful to
the public whom it is our duty to
protect.

Relations of Officers

The second appendix outlines the
functions of and deals with the re-
lations between the commissioner and
deputy commissioner of the new
force. The third appendix provides
for the establishment of a Reserve
Unit to suppress riots, disturbances
and labour troubles. The personnel
of the unit consists of an officer-in-
charge, a deputy officer, three officers
in charge of squads, two clerks, nine
sergeants and 62 constables totalling
78 men. When called out to quell a
disturbance members of the unit will
be accompanied by foreign and
Japanese members of its foreign
affairs branch.

The duties of the unit will include
its operation in emergency cases,
maintenance of order on any locality
where trouble breaks out, arrest of
robbers and bandits, search of pejes
and reinforcement of police
stations. The unit will carry batons,
rifles and will be trained in riot drill
and its transport will be equipped
with axes and crowbars for breaking
doors.

The unit will operate under the
orders of the commissioner and direc-
tion of the deputy commissioner but
when despatched to divisions to as-
sist in its functions, will be placed
under the direction of the officer in
charge of the division concerned.

设立预备队的规定

此外还规定设立一支预备队，编制为78名警员和5名警官，该部队将在警务处处长的命令及副处长的指挥下行动。当奉命行动时，该部队将始终置于相关分区主管警官的指挥之下。新警察部队的部门包括：警务科、执行科、特务科、外事科、刑事科、督察科以及秘书室。未经市政府与上海公共租界工部局同意，不得改变该部队的编制人数。

除五个警察分区外，还将设立若干派出所和分所。各分区的辖区范围如下：

第一分区：北至苏州河，东至租界边界，南至兆丰公园路（不含），西至勃伦南地块（不含）。
第二分区：北至兆丰公园路（含），东至租界边界，南至海格路，西至爱丁堡路（含）。
第三分区：北至苏州河，东至勃伦南地块（含）及爱丁堡路（不含），南至愚园路（不含），西至铁路（不含）。
第四分区：北至愚园路（含），东至爱丁堡路（不含），西至大西路（含）。
第五分区：北至大西路（不含），东至爱丁堡路（不含）及海格路（含），南至虹桥（含），西至铁路（不含）。

由于总体局势动荡不安，铁路线以西的区域未予讨论。

加强警务合作

在阐述了各部门的职能及其人员配置后，协议规定，新警察部队与工部局警察之间应在提出请求且确有必要时相互提供协助，双方各设一名联络官及三名助理，负责情报交换、协调搜查及引渡嫌疑人，并协助圆满解决涉外案件。

根据协议，新警察部队的一部分职员，以及在居民多为外国人且在该区域拥有工厂、商店和产业的分区担任主管的警官，如认为必要，将从工部局推荐的候选人中任命。凡因行为不端而被工部局警察开除或辞职的警官或文员，均无资格受雇于新警察部队。此规定同样适用于此前被判刑事犯罪者或被法国警察开除者；同时，上海公共租界工部局警察亦不会雇用未来从新警察部队被开除的人员。中文为新警察部队的官方语言，用于其所有官方文件。

协议中包含三个附录，以及一份关于在新警察部队管辖区域内取缔非法营业的特别附件。第一个附录规定了新警察部队与租界警察之间的更密切合作，具体如下：

合作原则

附录一指出，出于公共利益，必须确保在一区域作案的罪犯无法在相邻区域获得庇护，因此建议就以下一般条款达成一致：

任何在西区作案后逃入租界，或反之亦然，并被紧追逮捕的人，仅会被带至逮捕地最近的警察局备案，并立即直接移交，相关警察越界执法不承担任何责任。

凡在租界内被发现持有从西特区盗窃的财物者，或反之亦然，一旦在相应警察局记录详情后，将立即移交给失窃地所属的警察部队。

在调查犯罪时，如果上海西区特别警察部队的成员发现犯罪团伙的同伙居住或藏匿在工部局警察管辖区域内，相关警察局将立即配合负责此类案件的警官，以实施对这些罪犯的逮捕。

对于下列犯罪，如有合理怀疑认为案情属实，被捕人员将立即直接移交：武装绑架；诱拐；武装抢劫；抢劫；恐吓信；胁迫；谋杀或谋杀未遂。

在西区作案的人员应直接移交上海地方法院，依法处理。

对于较轻罪行的嫌疑人直接移交，将依据公共利益及现有证据决定。

在执行上述规定时，很大程度上取决于善意以及联合打击犯罪分子的真诚愿望，必须努力遵循该谅解的精神及条文，而任何企图滥用这些合作条款的行为，只会导致损害我们要保护之公众利益的局面。

警官之间的关系

第二个附录概述了新警察部队警务处处长与副处长的职能，并处理两者之间的关系。第三个附录规定设立一支预备队，以镇压暴动、骚乱和劳资纠纷。该部队人员包括一名主管警官、一名副主管警官、三名小队主管警官、两名文员、九名巡长和62名巡捕，共计78人。当被召去平息骚乱时，该部队成员将由其外事科的外籍和日本籍成员陪同。

该部队的职责包括在紧急情况下行动，在任何发生骚乱的地区维持秩序，逮捕盗匪，搜查僻静处（pejes）[原文不清，疑为僻静角落或特定地点]，以及增援警察局。该部队将配备警棍和步枪，并接受防暴操练，其运输车辆将配备斧头和撬棍，用于破门。

该部队将在警务处处长的命令及副处长的指挥下行动，但当被派往各分区协助执行任务时，将置于相关分区主管警官的指挥之下。

Western Area Police
Pact Signed—“To End
Outside Roads Crimes”

Heralding the “immediate” cessation of the state of lawless confusion that has been reigning in the Western areas since the hostilities swept over the city three years ago, a “full and detailed” agreement for the establishment of a Special Police Force to administer the territory was signed by Chairman W. J. Keswick of the Shanghai Municipal Council and Mayor Chen Kung-po of the Shanghai Municipal Government at the Civic Center, Kiangwan, at 10 a.m. yesterday.

Sitting at a long table in the main hall of the Civic Center’s Administration Building, surrounded by a battery of Chinese, Japanese and foreign newspapermen and photographers, Mr. Keswick and Mayor Chen Kung-po signed many documents to the flash of dozens of flash bulbs.

Mr. Keswick sat with his arm still in a sling, a souvenir of the Special Meeting of Ratepayers held at the Race Club recently. Two copies of the agreement one in Chinese and the other in English were signed. Champagne toasts were drunk. Hand-shakes were exchanged. The gathering broke up in a cordial atmosphere.

1,446 Officers Wanted

The signing of the agreement, which creates a police force of 1,446 men to administer the western areas adjacent to the Settlement and Concession, brings to a close two years of protracted negotiations, postponements and unpleasant incidents.

The establishment of the police force is promised “immediately.” The state of affairs that has kept the area a haven of refuge for murderers, fugitives from justice, vice, opium and gambling dens will be ripped off “as soon as the police force is organized and established.”

As reported by THE CHINA PRESS on Saturday, the agreement signed yesterday follows the lines of the agreement reached between Major K. M. Bourne of the S.M.P. and Colonel Loo Ying of the Municipal Government Police a few months ago.

Close Co-operation

One of the main features of the police force embodied in the agreement is that cases involving foreign nationals will be handled by foreign members of the police force. An appendix to the agreement also provides for close co-operation between the “Western Area Special Police Force” (as the new force will be called) and the S.M.P.

It provides for the pursuit, without hindrance, from one area into another in cases of serious crimes. “Immediate co-operation” is envisaged when arrests are required. Armed kidnappers, abductors, armed robbers, robbers, intimidators, murderers and attempted would-be murderers will be handed over direct at once if there is reasonable suspicion that a true case exists.”

The police force in charge of the whole area will be divided into five police divisions. The hats of members of the force will be adorned with a badge bearing “distinctive characters” denoting “Special Police.” There will be a Chinese Commissioner and a European Deputy Commissioner.

Cases To Be Referred

Cases involving foreign nationals will be handled under the instructions of the latter, who will be nominated by the S.M.C. If any doubt arises as to the proper handling of a case, the Commissioner and Deputy Commissioner, if unable to agree, will refer the matter to the Commissioner of the S.M.P. and Commissioner of the Municipal Government, failing this, to the Mayor and the Chairman of the Council.

Cases involving foreign nationals with extraterritorial rights will be handled according to the national laws concerned. In other cases, Chinese law will be applied. Persons committing crimes in the Western area will be handed over direct to the Shanghai District Court.

Ruled by “the public interest,” however, will be the direct handing over of suspects in less serious crimes. “Much will depend on goodwill and a sincere desire to combine against the criminal element,” according to the agreement,

“and every effort must be made to follow the spirit as well as the letter of the understanding.”

Up To Railway

Not administrated by the new police force, according to the agreement, is territory to the West of the railway line. This is explained as being due to the “general unsettled situation.”

Not permitted to join the Police force will be “police officers or clerks previously dismissed or resigned from the Shanghai Municipal Police for improper conduct. No jail-birds will be taken in either. The Terms of Service of employees nominated by the S.M.C. will remain unaltered.

Envisaged in the agreement is the formation of Reserve Unit, comprising 5 officers and 78 men, to suppress riots, and operating under the orders of the Commissioner and the direction of the Deputy Commissioner. When sent out to reinforce a Division it will be placed under the direction of the Officer In-Charge of the Division.

Taxes Unmentioned

Not mentioned in the agreement is the setting up of an independent revenue department to collect taxes in the Western area—a separate bureau described by Mayor Chen Kung-po in a press conference held six weeks ago. The taxes collected by this bureau were to go towards the maintenance of the joint police force and other expenses in the area. Like the police force, it was to be governed by the Municipal Government, despite joint control with the Settlement.

Yesterday’s agreement is preceded by a temporary settlement reached between the late Mayor Fu Siao-en and Cornell S. Franklin, former Chairman of the S.M.C. nearly a year ago. Last year’s agreement was preceded by more than a year of promised “agreements” which never quite reached a point where both sides were willing to sit down and sign their names on the dotted line.

Relations between the two bodies were strained on many occasions. On October 20, 1939 a Chinese policeman was shot dead and a Sikh was wounded when “intimidation by force” climaxed demands for control of a traffic post in the Western area. On the morning of January 6, 1940, G. Godfrey Phillips, Secretary-General of the S.M.C. miraculously escaped from a bullet-ridden car, unscathed. The assassins, on their part, escaped too.

西区警务
协定签署——“终结越界筑路区域犯罪”

为宣告自三年前战火席卷全市以来一直笼罩西区的无法无天混乱状态“立即”终止，上海公共租界工部局董事会主席 W. J. Keswick 先生与上海特别市政府市长陈公博于昨日上午十时在江湾市中心签署了关于组建一支特别警察部队以管理该区域的“全面且详细”的协定。

Keswick 先生与陈公博市长坐在市中心行政大楼主厅的一张长桌旁，在大批中、日及外籍记者和摄影师的包围下，伴随着数十个闪光灯的不断闪烁，签署了许多文件。

Keswick 先生的手臂仍吊着绷带，这是最近在跑马厅举行的纳税人特别会议留下的纪念。协定的中文和英文文本各两份均获签署。众人举杯共饮香槟。双方握手致意。集会在融洽的气氛中结束。

需招募 1,446 名警员

该协定的签署标志着为期两年的漫长谈判、拖延和不愉快事件的终结，协定规定组建一支由 1,446 人组成的警察部队，以管理与租界及法租界相邻的西区。

警察部队的组建被承诺将“立即”进行。那种使该区域成为谋杀犯、逃犯、卖淫、鸦片馆和赌博窝点避难所的状况，将在“警察部队组织建立完成后”被彻底清除。

正如《字林西报》（THE CHINA PRESS）周六所报道，昨日签署的协定遵循了几个月前工部局警务处 K. M. Bourne 少校与市政府警察局陆英（Loo Ying，音译）上校之间达成的协定路线。

密切合作

协定中所体现的警察部队的主要特点之一是，涉及外国人的案件将由警察部队中的外籍成员处理。协定的附录还规定，“西区特别警察部队”（新部队的名称）与工部局警务处（S.M.P.）之间将进行密切合作。

协定规定，在严重犯罪案件中，追捕行动可以不受阻碍地从一个区域进入另一个区域。当需要逮捕时，设想进行“即时合作”。如果有合理怀疑表明案件属实，武装绑匪、绑架者、武装抢劫犯、抢劫犯、恐吓者、谋杀犯以及谋杀未遂者将直接立即移交。”

负责整个区域的警察部队将分为五个警区。部队成员的帽子上将饰有标明“特别警察”的“独特字符”徽章。将设有一名华籍总监和一名欧籍副总监。

案件移送

涉及外国人的案件将在后者的指示下处理，后者由工部局董事会提名。如果对案件的适当处理产生任何疑问，总监和副总监若无法达成一致，应将事项提交给工部局警务处处长和市政府警察局局长；若仍无法解决，则提交给市长和董事会主席。

涉及享有治外法权的外国人的案件，将根据相关国家法律处理。在其他案件中，将适用中国法律。在西区犯罪的人员将直接移交给上海地方法院。

然而，对于较轻罪行的嫌疑人，其直接移交将受“公共利益”支配。根据协定，“这在很大程度上取决于善意以及联合打击犯罪分子的真诚愿望”，

“并且必须尽一切努力遵循该谅解的精神及其文字规定。”

直至铁路线

根据协定，铁路线以西的区域不由新警察部队管理。这被解释为是由于“总体局势动荡不安”。

“此前因行为不当而被上海公共租界工部局警务处开除或辞职的警官或职员”不得加入该警察部队。也不得录用任何有前科的罪犯。由工部局董事会提名的雇员的任职条件将保持不变。

协定中设想组建一支预备队，由 5 名警官和 78 名警员组成，用于镇压骚乱，并在总监的命令和副总监的指导下行动。当被派去增援某个警区时，它将置于该警区负责人的指挥之下。

未提及税收

协定中未提及在西区设立独立的税务部门以征收税款——这是陈公博市长在六周前举行的新闻发布会上描述的一个独立机构。该局征收的税款将用于维持联合警察部队及该区域的其他开支。与警察部队一样，尽管与租界共同管理，但它将由市政府管辖。

昨日的协定之前，是已故市长傅筱庵与工部局前董事会主席 Cornell S. Franklin 在近一年前达成的临时解决方案。去年的协定之前则是长达一年多承诺的“协定”，但这些协定从未真正达到双方愿意坐下来在虚线上签字的程度。

双方机构之间的关系曾多次紧张。1939 年 10 月 20 日，当“武力恐吓”达到要求控制西区一个交通岗亭的高潮时，一名中国警察被枪杀，一名锡克教警察受伤。1940 年 1 月 6 日上午，工部局秘书长 G. Godfrey Phillips 奇迹般地从一辆布满弹孔的汽车中逃脱，毫发无损。刺客方面也已逃脱。

Gambling Suppressed By
New Accord For Policing
Of The Western District

New Era Of Law And Order Should Be Ushered In
Under Terms Of Agreement For Joint Policing
By S.M.C. And Shanghai Municipal Government

SPECIAL JOINT POLICE FORCE TO BE
ESTABLISHED IN NEAR FUTURE

Culminating almost a year of negotiations, an agreement was signed at the Civic Centre at Kiangwan at 10 o'clock yesterday morning, creating the Western Shanghai Area Special Police Force, under joint administration of the Police Bureau of the Shanghai Municipal Government and the S. M. P.

The new special force, to have absolute authority in the Western Area, representing the extra-Settlement roads district, will commence to function as soon as details can be worked out by General Loo Ying, Commissioner of the Police Bureau of the Shanghai Municipal Government, and Major K. M. Bourne, M.C., Commissioner of the S. M. P., possibly within this month.

One of the most important results of the new arrangement, which will be accompanied by the withdrawal from the area in question of all other police, will be the pledge to close all nefarious establishments in this section, including gambling houses, enterprises engaged in drug traffic, etc.

Five Police Stations

Five police stations will be maintained in the area, with a force of 1,446 men, of whom 197 are to be appointed by the S.M.P., including both high officials and constables. In general, all cases involving foreigners will be handled by European officers, while mutual rights of pursuit from the adjacent areas have been agreed upon. A Reserve Unit will be maintained, comprising a total of 83 effectives.

The agreement, in general, consolidates the main provisions of the modus vivendi signed on February 16 of last year, which empowered the heads of the respective Chinese and International police forces to negotiate the agreement now signed by Mr. W. J. Keswick, Chairman of the S.M.C., and Mayor Chen Kung-po, of the Shanghai Municipal Government.

Complete Harmony

The significant agreement was signed with due ceremony, sealed by a toast in champagne, in the presence of leading officials of both the Chinese and International Administrations at the Headquarters of the Shanghai Municipal Government. With his left arm in a sling but bearing no other apparent marks of his near-tragic experience when he was shot in the performance of his duties at the recent Special Rate-payers' meeting, Mr. Keswick arrived shortly before the appointed hour, accompanied by Mr. G. Godfrey Phillips, Secretary and Commissioner General of the S.M.C., Major K. M. Bourne, S.M.P. Commissioner, Mr. R. T. Bryan, Jr., S.M.C. advocate, Mr. K. Ibusuki, Japanese Deputy Secretary of the S.M.C., and Mr. T. Beesley, Assistant Secretary of the S.M.C.

Mayor Chen Kung-po was attended by General Lu Yang, Commissioner of the Special Municipality Police Bureau, and Mr. Kimpson-yu, Secretary-General of the Shanghai Municipal Government. A cordial atmosphere prevailed throughout.

The document was prepared in two copies, one in English and the other in Chinese, each signed by both Mayor Chen and Mr. Keswick.

Chinese Commissioner

Heading the new force will be a Chinese Commissioner and a European Deputy Commissioner, the latter to be nominated by the Shanghai Municipal Council. Cases of doubt regarding partition of responsibility will first be referred to the Commissioner and Deputy Commissioner, and if they fail to agree, then to the Commissioners of the S.M.P. and Shanghai Municipal Government Police.

The special force will be composed of the existing Police Main Corps, the entire West Shanghai Division and the officers of the Detective Branch Corps, together with officers recommended by the S.M.C. In general, it will patrol the former West Shanghai Division and a section under the jurisdiction of the Zikawei Police Division.

The Divisional Branches are as follows:—

1st Division
Soochow Creek on the north, Settlement Boundary on the east, Jessfield Road (exclusive) on the south, Brenan Piece (exclusive) on the west.

2nd Division
Jessfield Road (inclusive) on the north, Settlement Boundary on the east, Avenue Haig on the south, Edinburgh Road (inclusive) on the west.

3rd Division
Soochow Creek on the north, Brenan Piece (inclusive) and Edinburgh Road (exclusive) on the east, Yu Yuen Road (exclusive) on the south, Railway (exclusive) on the west.

4th Division
Yu Yuen Road (inclusive) on the north, Edinburgh Road (exclusive) on the east, Great Western Road (inclusive) on the west.

5th Division
Great Western Road (exclusive) on the north, Edinburgh Road (exclusive) and Avenue Haig (inclusive) on the east, Hungjao (inclusive) on the south, Railway (exclusive) on the west.

The area to the west of the railway line will not be discussed owing to the general unsettled situation.

The new force will be divided into the following branches: Police Affairs, Executive, Special (dealing with the suppression of Communism, publication of inflammatory literature, etc.), Foreign Affairs, Crime, Supervising and Secretariat.

In Foreign Areas

In areas where there are important foreign interests, including both settlers and property-holders, special consideration will be given to the appointment of foreign officers and constables, under a prescribed plan.

Cases involving foreign nationals will be handled by the Foreign Affairs Branch and other foreign officers, under the instructions of the Deputy Commissioner and in accordance with the foreign laws concerned. With regard to foreigners who do not enjoy Consular privileges, Chinese law will apply.

Included in the foreign personnel numbering 197 will be, in addition to officers already mentioned, a Deputy Commissioner in the Foreign Affairs Branch, a European Officer-in-charge and 27 Junior Officers, including nine Japanese; in the General Affairs Branch a Japanese Deputy in charge and two Junior Officers (one Chinese and one Westerner); in the Administration Branch two Junior Officers (one Japanese and one Westerner); in the Special Branch a Japanese Deputy in charge and two Junior Officers (one Japanese and one Westerner); in the Supervising Branch a Western Deputy in charge and two Junior Officers (one Chinese and one Japanese).

In the five Police Divisions the Shanghai Municipal Council will nominate two Officers-in-Charge and three Deputies, and in addition 23 Sub-Inspectors, 16 Sergeants and 110 Chinese constables.

Chinese Language Official

Chinese shall be the official language for all documents. Uniforms of the City Government effectives shall be in accordance with the normal requirements of the Shanghai Municipal Police Bureau, with a distinctive hat badge worn by all members, signifying in Chinese and English, "Special Police." Uniforms of the Japanese and Western members will be decided later. Accommodation will be provided for their respective units by the Shanghai Municipal Government and the S.M.P.

Special provisions are made for close co-operation, pursuit and the following up of serious crime. Division of the responsibilities of the Commissioner and Deputy-Commissioner is specially set forth in an appendix. The functions of the Reserve Unit are to take care of special disturbances. It will be subject to orders of the Commissioner.

Suppress Gambling

Appended as a special annex is a clause, epoch-making in its significance, virtually striking a death-blow at nefarious practices in the Extra-Settlement Roads area, long a vexed and contentious question. It reads:

As soon as the Western Shanghai Area Special Police Force has been organized and established and commences to function in accordance with the Chinese law, all illegitimate businesses (such as the running of gambling dens, trafficking in opium and narcotics and providing addicts with such narcotics) shall be forbidden to exist within the area under its jurisdiction.

"All illegitimate and unlawful businesses shall be ordered to cease with the inauguration of the Western Shanghai Area Special Police Force and the commencement of the discharge of its functions. Any attempt to resume such activities shall at once be strictly suppressed."

近期将建立特别联合警察部队

经过近一年的谈判，昨天上午10时，在江湾市中心签署了一项协议，成立上海西区特别警察部队，由上海市政府警察局和工部局警务处（S. M. P.）共同管理。

这支新的特别部队将在西区拥有绝对权力，代表越界筑路区域，一旦上海市政府警察局局长陆英将军和工部局警务处处长K. M. Bourne少校（M.C.）制定出细节，该部队即开始运作，可能在本月内。

新安排的最重要成果之一，伴随着所有其他警察从该区域撤出，是承诺关闭该地区的所有非法场所，包括赌场、从事毒品交易的企业等。

五个警察局

该区域将维持五个警察局，警力为1,446人，其中197人由工部局任命，包括高级官员和巡捕。一般而言，涉及外国人的案件将由欧美警官处理，同时已就相邻区域的相互追捕权达成协议。将维持一支预备队，共计83名有效人员。

该协议总体上巩固了去年2月16日签署的临时协定的主要条款，该协定授权中外警察部队负责人谈判现在由工部局总董W. J. Keswick先生和上海市长陈公博签署的协议。

完全和谐

这项重要的协议在上海市政府总部，在中外行政当局主要官员的见证下，以适当的仪式签署，并以香槟祝酒 sealed。Keswick先生在最近的特别纳税人会议上执行公务时遭枪击，经历了近乎悲剧的经历，左臂吊着绷带，但身上没有其他明显的伤痕，他在预定时间前不久到达，陪同他的有工部局秘书长兼总办G. Godfrey Phillips先生、工部局警务处处长K. M. Bourne少校、工部局法律顾问R. T. Bryan, Jr.先生、工部局日本副秘书Ibusuki K.先生以及工部局助理秘书T. Beesley先生。

陈公博市长由特别市警察局局长卢英将军和上海市政府秘书长俞鸿钧先生陪同。整个过程气氛融洽。

文件准备了两份，一份英文，一份中文，均由陈市长和Keswick先生签署。

中方局长

新部队将由一名中方局长和一名欧方副局长领导，后者由上海公共租界工部局提名。关于责任划分的疑案，首先提交给局长和副局长，如果他们无法达成一致，则提交给工部局警务处处长和上海市政府警察局局长。

特别部队将由现有的警察主力团、整个上海西区分部以及侦探支队的军官组成，再加上工部局推荐的军官。一般而言，它将巡逻原上海西区分部和徐家汇警察分部管辖的一部分区域。

各分部如下：—

第一分部
北至苏州河，东至租界边界，南至兆丰公园路（不含），西至Brenan Piece（不含）。

第二分部
北至兆丰公园路（含），东至租界边界，南至海格路，西至爱丁堡路（含）。

第三分部
北至苏州河，东至Brenan Piece（含）和爱丁堡路（不含），南至愚园路（不含），西至铁路（不含）。

第四分部
北至愚园路（含），东至爱丁堡路（不含），西至大西路（含）。

第五分部
北至大西路（不含），东至爱丁堡路（不含）和海格路（含），南至虹桥（含），西至铁路（不含）。

由于总体局势动荡，铁路线以西的区域不予讨论。

新部队将分为以下部门：警务处、执行处、特别处（负责镇压共产主义、出版煽动性文献等）、外事处、刑事处、督察处和秘书处。

在外侨区域

在既有定居者又有财产持有者等重要外国利益的区域，将根据规定计划，在任命外国警官和巡捕时给予特别考虑。

涉及外国国民的案件将由外事处和其他外国警官在副局长的指示下，并根据相关外国法律处理。对于不享有领事特权的外国人，适用中国法律。

在197名外籍人员中，除上述官员外，还包括：外事处一名副局长、一名欧籍主管和27名初级警官（其中包括9名日本人）；总务处一名日本副主管和两名初级警官（一名中国人和一名西方人）；行政处两名初级警官（一名日本人和一名西方人）；特别处一名日本副主管和两名初级警官（一名日本人和一名西方人）；督察处一名西方副主管和两名初级警官（一名中国人和一名日本人）。

在五个警察分部中，上海公共租界工部局将提名两名主管和三名副手，此外还有23名副巡官、16名警长和110名华籍巡捕。

中文为官方语言

所有文件均以中文为官方语言。市政府有效人员的制服应符合上海市政府警察局的正常要求，所有成员佩戴独特的帽徽，用中英文标明“特别警察”。日籍和西籍成员的制服稍后决定。上海市政府和工部局警务处将为其各自单位提供住宿。

另有特别规定，旨在密切合作、追捕和跟进严重犯罪。局长和副局长的职责分工在附录中特别列明。预备队的职能是处理特殊骚乱。它将受局长命令的约束。

取缔赌博

作为特别附件附上的是一项具有时代意义的条款，实际上对长期以来令人烦恼和争议的越界筑路区域的非法行为给予了致命打击。条款内容如下：

一旦上海西区特别警察部队组建成立并开始依据中国法律运作，其管辖区域内禁止存在所有非法业务（如经营赌场、贩卖鸦片和麻醉品以及向吸毒者提供此类麻醉品）。

“随着上海西区特别警察部队的成立及其职能的开始履行，所有非法和违法业务将被责令停止。任何试图恢复此类活动的行为都将立即受到严厉镇压。”

APPENDIX I. 
AGREEMENT 


For Close Cooperation Against The Criminal Element Between The Western 
Shanghai Area Special Police Force And The Shanghai Municipal Polices. 


As it is essential in the public interest that criminals who commit crimes in one area, 
do not obtain safety in an adjacent area, it is suggested the following general provisions be agreed 
upon :— 


Close Pursuit: 


Any person committing a crime in the Western area, who runs or escapes into the 
Settlement or vice versa, and is closely pursued and arrested, will be taken to the nearest Police 
Station of the area in wKich the arrest is made for record only, and will be handed over direct 
and at once, while the Police concerned will be held in no way to blame for crossing the boundary. 


Possession of Property Stolen: 


Any person found in the Settlement in possession of property stolen from the Western 
Special Area, or vice versa, will be handed over to the Police Force controlling the area in which 
the property was stolen at once, as soon as particulars have been recorded at the appropriate 
Police Station. 


Following up Cases of Serious Crime: 


In the investigation of crimé, when it is found by members of the Western Shanghai 
Area Special Police Force that confederates of a criminal gang are living or hiding in the area 
under the jurisdiction of the Municipal Police, the Police Station concerned will give immediate 
cooperation to the Officers in charge of such cases to effect the arrests of such criminals. 


In the case of the following crimes, such persons when arrested will be handed over 
direct at once if there is reasonable suspicion that a true case exists :— 


Armed Kidnapping; Abduction; Armed Robbery; Robbery; Threatening Letters; In- 
timidation; Murder or Attempted Murder. 


- The Western Shanghai Area Special Police Force will, within one week, report details of 
evidence against such accused to the Shanghai Municipal Police or will return accused to the 
custody of the Municipal Police or vice versa. 


The Western Shanghai Area Special Police orce will afford similar facilities to the 
Shanghai Municipal Police under exactly similar conditions. 


Such prisoners will, in every case, receive proper treatment within the law, and be re- 
turned, if not charged, in good condition. Such prisoners will not be detained more than 24 hours 
without going to Court. 7 


Persons committing crimes in the Western Area shall be handed over direct to the 
Shanghai District Court to be dealt with according to law. 


Following Up Other Crimes: 


The direct handling over of suspects in less serious crimes will be ruled by the public 
interest, and in accordance with the evidence available. 


In carrying out the above, much will depend on goodwill and a sincere desire to combine 
against the criminal element and every effort must be made to follow the spirit as well as the 
“letter of the understanding, while any attempt to misuse these provisions for cooperation can 
only result in a state of affairs harmful to the public whom it is our duty to protect.

After an interval of just cne year the 
modus vivendi concerning the policing of 
the Western Area, which was reached last 
February, has been supplemented by a full 
agreement between the Shanghai Municipal 
Government and the Shanghai Municipal’ 
Council, which it is hoped will settle once! 
and for all the many questions which have} 
been outstanding all too long, and establish’ 
means for restoring order in the ‘Badlands.’ 
The agreement goes into considerable de- 
tail regarding the formation of the new 
police force and a system has been evolved 
which should prove completely workable. 
Attached to the agreement are three appen- 
dices and one special anncx, which are of 
the utmost importance. In the first there 
is provision for ‘close pursuit” which 
reads :— 

Any person committing a crime in the 
Western Area, who runs, or escapes into the 
Settlement, or vice versa, and is closely 
pursued and arrested, will he taken to the 
nearest police station of the area in which 
the arrest is made for record only, and will 
be handed over direct and at once, while 
the Police concerned will be held in no way 
to blame for crossing the boundary. 

This important provision should serve to re- 
move difficulties which have arisen in the 
past out of conflict of police jurisdiction, 
and should serve to rob criminals of that 
asylum which could easily be secured mere-. 
ly by dodging across the boundaries. 

The same appendix provides for close co- 
operation in dealing with possession of 
stolen property and the following '» of 


serious cases of crime, and tends to give the’ 
Settlement and Western Area Police a de-'! 


gree of mobility which has hitherto not ex- 
isted, and while they will each maintain 
their separate identity, they will in fact 
become practically one single unit when 
dealing with criminals. This should ultim- 
ately have the cffect of putting a strangle—- 
hold on those criminals who, using the 
Western Area as their base, operate in the 
International Settlement taking refuge out- 
side the limits and making it dfficult for 
the Municipal Police to go after them. 

That will indeed be a welcome change, but 
the provisions of the special annex are even. 
more so :—

further delays in putting the scheme into 
operation, and that every effort will be made 
to bring the special police force into being 
as quickly as possible. That subversive 
elements may seek to prevent that being 
done may be taken for granted, but 
the worth of this most important document 
can only be measured by the manner in 
which its terms are carried out. If that is 
done to the bitter end, then a substantial 
reform will have been effected and the

ions are to be extended to Major K. M.

most useful,_whose signatures are now 
appended to the agreement. The removal of 
a frequent cause of misunderstandings in the
